text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to a survey of Australia's top companies undertaken by The Financial Review, shareholders in many companies in this country are having to wait more than four months to get their dividends, a delay that is costing corporate Australia close to A$1 million a day in interest savings. Page 1.

In a bid to fend off the Internet market push from Optus, Telstra will unveil a new line of Internet products targeting both small business and large corporates under the "Big Pond" brand name. One of the new products to be launched on Wednesday will be business Dial, which offers small and medium-sized businesses an Internet dial-up service with invoice billing capability. Page 3.

Australian Bureau of Statistics retail trade figures released last Friday showed the volume of turnover in stores was up only 0.6 per cent in the three months to September, providing further provocation for the Reserve Bank to lower overnight cash rates at its regular monthly board meeting tomorrow. Page 5.

The New South Wales Government has decided to award the purchaser of Axiom Funds Management an exclusive five-year contract to manage the A$17 billion in superannuation savings of the State's public servants. The Government will release an abridged version of a positive report into the funds manager as
the prelude to Axiom being put up for sale by tender. Page 19.
There seems little chance of an Optus
Communications
sharemarket listing this year following the
Federal Government's
decision to deny major foreign shareholders increased voting
power. Bellsouth of the US and UK group Cable &
Wireless have expressed conern that under existing laws an Australian shareholder with as little as 10 per cent of the company could hold the balance of power at Optus. Page 19.

French utility Lyonnaise des Eaux has set up a A$380 million fund with Lend Lease Corporation and other investors, Asia Water Holdings Fund, to build projects for clean water in South-East Asia and plans to invest more than A$300 million in water filtration and treatment plants in Australia. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to Reserve Bank research which supports a call by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello for the major banks to cut their standard home lending rates without waiting for a further easing in official monetary policy, banks could slash their standard vaiable mortgage rates from 9.25 per cent to 8.5 per cent if they adopted margins that are common internationally. Page 3.

In a move expected to trigger the start of the C$700 million construction of Canada's first diamond mine, BHP has gained the "full support" of the Canadian Government to go ahead with the A$1.1 billion development of Lac de Gras, the company's diamond proect in Canada's North-West Territories. Page 29.

Proposals from the Small Business Deregulation Taskforce could see big increases in fringe benefits tax for companies with long-distance car fleets, with the new rate expected to be almost double the present seven per cent FBT rate applying for cars traveling more than 40,000 kilometres a year. Page 31.
that could mean long-term growth or financial ruin. Page 31.

The National Farmers Federation has joined the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association in seeking assurances from Prime Minister John Howard that their industries will not be subjected to the same cuts to the diesel fuel rebate scheme as miners, claiming measures announced last week would take away most of their rebate entitlements. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Colonial Group's funds management arm, Colonial Investment Management Ltd, has bought BZW Investment Management Ltd's 13.75 per cent interest in CH China Investments Ltd, singling CH China out as a potential vehicle for Colonial's thrust into Asia. Pge 31.

Agreeing to chair the Family Business Council, influential businessman David Smorgon said yesterday the ability of small business to deal with issues such as succession, mediation and relationships with non-family members of staff were major issues

If Thursday's employment figures are weak and the Reserve Bank announces it is as pessimistic about Australia's immediate economic outlook as most economists, a widely-tipped reduction in official interest rates on Wednesday will be accompanied by another rate cut early next year. Page 37.

After last week confirming that its share of the local beer market had slipped by 1.4 points to 42 per cent in the year to August, Lion Nathan chief executive Douglas Myers has conceded the brewing and soft drink giant's brands needed refocussing. Page 37

Although there is still a good chance the float of Optus Communications will not go ahead this year at all, any new capital needed by the company will have to come from existing shareholders in a rights issue and any new public shareholders will come from 25 per cent shareholder Mayne Nickless' share register, because any new capital raising from the public would be too expensive. Page 37.

Although rumours abound that foreign banks are closely examining Australia's major banks for acquisitions after the completion of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, Morgan Stanley's Hong Kong-based analyst, John Hobson, says the economies of Latin America and Asia are the priorities for most global banks. Page 39.

According to a new study from finance industry researcher Assirt, the retail managed funds industry has recorded its strongest sales quarter since Assirt began issuing reports in 1990, with falling Australian bank interest rates and improving
sentiment enouraging investors to turn to cash management trusts and "growth assets". Page 39.

The Victorian Government is set to split Gas & Fuel into three companies ready for sale, in a deal that would probably net well over A$1 billion from foreign bidders, including new owners of the privatised electricity distributors and from local buyers suh as the Sydney-based AGL . Page 39.
THE AGE

The Australian Rice Growers Cooperative started selling New South Wales-grown Koshihikari rice into a select number of Tokyo supermarkets this month, offering the variety for A$22 a bag, compared to the A$36 charge for a Japanese-grown bag of Koshihikari However, the Australian variety goes on sale in Japan about four months after harvest, when it has lost some of its fresh taste and shiny appearance. Page C1.

A deal over the A$3 billion Bass Strait resource rent tax dispute with Esso XON.AX , BHP and the Federal Government, and the signing of new contracts for Bass Strait should clear the way for the Victorian Government to split Gas and Fuel into three companies read for sale. Page C1.

A new study by industry researcher Assirt reveals the retail managed funds industry has recorded its strongest sales quarter since 1990, with A$2.66 billion flowing into the funds during the September quarter, bringing the year's total to A$6.22 billion. Page C3.

The Australian petroleum industry claims late Cabinet changes to eligibility for the diesel fuel rebate scheme will cost it up to A$30 million a year and the National Farmers Federation has warned the Government it would be "appalled" if the mining industy's deal was extended to the rural sector. Page C3.

The chairman of the Federal Government's inquiry into the financial sector, Stan Wallis, said yesterday he has divested his shareholdings in the bank sector and has instructed other inquiry members to do the same. Wallis retired as managing director of paper and packaging giant Amcor after 19 years to become chairman of the banking inquiry. Page C3.

Some observers believe the Reserve Bank of Australia board will decide to cut official interest rates on Wednesday, while others expect a rates reduction will be delayed until December. Commonwealth Bank of Australia economist Michael Workman says
"the hurdles that the Reserve Bank put in the way of an easing have been met", clearing the way for a cut by 50 basis points. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
